title: Documentation support (MEAT) for chronic conditions
question: Which chronic condition, if any, is supported for risk adjustment by this note? Choose 'no code' if none is supported.
note:
Chief Complaint
The patient is a 79-year-old female presenting for evaluation of persistent low back pain.

HPI
The patient reports a 3-month history of aching pain in her lower back. She describes the sensation as a dull, constant ache that occasionally sharpens with prolonged standing or walking. She notes that the pain is most severe at the end of the day. She denies any recent falls, trauma, or radiating pain into her lower extremities. She has attempted to manage the discomfort with over-the-counter heat packs and rest, which provide only minimal relief. She is seeking a consultation to discuss further management options and physical therapy.

Review of Systems
The patient denies chest pain, shortness of breath, fever, chills, or recent weight changes. She denies any numbness or tingling in her feet. She denies any changes in bowel or bladder function.

Social History
The patient is retired and lives in a single-story home with her spouse. She enjoys gardening and walking in her neighborhood. She denies tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History
The patient’s mother had a history of osteoarthritis. Her father had a history of hypertension.

Recent Labs
Hemoglobin: 12.4 g/dL
White Blood Cell Count: 7.2 x 10^9/L
Platelet Count: 210 x 10^9/L
eGFR: 78 mL/min/1.73m2

Vitals
Temperature: 98.6 F
Blood Pressure: 128/82 mmHg
Heart Rate: 72 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
Oxygen Saturation: 98% on room air
Height: 5'4"
Weight: 155 lbs

Medication List
Lisinopril 10 mg daily
Tirotium 18 mcg inhaled daily
Atorvastatin 20 mg daily
Albuterol as needed

Problem List
Status post cholecystectomy
Status post appendectomy
History of tonsillectomy

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. She appears in no acute distress. Physical exam of the spine reveals mild tenderness to palpation over the lumbar region. Range of motion of the lumbar spine is slightly limited by discomfort. No spinal step-offs are noted. Strength and sensation are intact in all lower extremities. Deep tendon reflexes are 2+ bilaterally.

Assessment
The patient is presenting with symptoms consistent with mechanical low back pain. There are no neurological deficits noted at this time.

Plan
The patient will begin a supervised physical therapy program focusing on core strengthening and stretching. We discussed the use of prescribed NSAIDs for acute flare-ups. She will follow up in four weeks to assess progress with physical therapy.

Electronically signed, D. Kowalski, NP, 05/14/2026
explanations: An inhaler on the medication list does not establish COPD; coders do not infer diagnoses from medications.

distractors.why: Only the provider can document a diagnosis.
